newsitem.title: USA: Edsel Ford II says he has no plans to change jobs.
newsitem.headline: Edsel Ford II says he has no plans to change jobs.

text.p: Edsel Ford II said Tuesday he has no plans to leave his job as president and chief operating officer of Ford Motor Co.'s Ford Credit unit, contradicting a published report in the Detroit News.

Through a spokeswoman, Ford said he was happy in his position at Ford Credit and was not going to replace Thomas Wagner as vice president of customer satisfaction for the automaker, as the newspaper had reported Tuesday.

The News, citing unnamed sources, said the move was expected to be announced in October. Edsel Ford was at the company's dealer introduction show in San Diego, Calif., and could not be reached directly for comment.
Earlier, Ford spokeswoman Pam Kueber declined to comment on the story, adding "We're not going to contribute to speculation."
Edsel Ford, 48, is the great-grandson of company founder Henry Ford, and the son of Henry Ford II, who ran the company from 1945 to 1980.

He is one of three Ford family members who sit on the automaker's board of directors, and the only one to work in senior management ranks. The Ford family controls 40 percent of the firm's voting stock.
Edsel Ford has worked at Ford Motor Co. since 1974, holding a variety of sales and marketing positions before being named president of Ford Credit in 1991.
Ford Credit is the largest unit within Ford's Financial Services Group, providing financing for a variety of Ford customers, and offering various insurance and other financial service products.

Edsel Ford has presided over a time of strong profits, international expansion and at Ford Credit. However, higher credit losses and lower margins from increasing depreciation expenses on leased vehicles have reduced the unit's earnings this year.
Ford's stock ended unchanged at $40.69 on the New York Stock Exchange.
